plc.heading: PLC code
plc.intro: Paste IEC 61131-3 Structured Text. It is checked for syntax errors, undeclared or unused tags, type mismatches and unreachable code, each shown on its line. Nothing is stored.
plc.label: Structured Text
plc.placeholder:
PROGRAM Main
  VAR
    Start : BOOL;
  END_VAR
  ...
END_PROGRAM
plc.rejected: That program could not be checked.
plc.failed: The check could not run. Try again.
plc.emptyResult: Findings appear here, each beside the line it is on.
plc.generateIntro: Describe what the program should do. The model writes it, and the same parser that checks pasted code checks it — the verdict comes with the code.
plc.describePlaceholder: e.g. Start/stop a conveyor motor: start button, normally-closed stop and E-stop, seal-in, run lamp.
plc.generatedNote: Written by a model and checked by the parser. Review it, and test it offline, before it runs on equipment.
plc.emptyGenerated: The generated program appears here, with its check.
plc.generateRejected: That program could not be generated. Try describing it differently.

review.intro: Sign in with a reviewer account to work your queue. Each item is labelled against its source; a correct label publishes it.

stale.empty: No live document has changed upstream.
stale.supersededHelp: The source now serves a different file from the one verified. Its passages are still live. Compare the two; if the change does not affect them, dismiss this with a note.
stale.withdrawnHelp: The source no longer serves this document (404 or 410). Its passages are still live until someone retracts them.
stale.notePlaceholder: e.g. Cover page and revision date only; ratings unchanged.
stale.dismissFailed: The dismissal was not saved. Try again.
stale.retractWarning: Every passage from this document leaves live answers now. Engineers asking about it will be told there is no verified source, until a new revision is reviewed. This is recorded with your name and note.

search.intro: Look up a fault code, a parameter or a wiring detail directly. Every result is a passage a reviewer verified, with a link to the page it came from.

calc.heading: Cable sizing
calc.intro: Size a copper or aluminium feeder from the IEC 60364-5-52 tables as ABB's installation handbook publishes them. Every figure names the table and page it came from; an input the tables do not cover is refused, not guessed.

method.C: C — clipped direct to a wall
method.E: E — multi-core in free air / on a tray
method.F: F — single-core in free air / on a tray

calc.title: Calculations

vfd.intro: Pick an ABB ACS880-01 drive for a motor on a 380-500 V or 660-690 V supply. The motor current is worked out from its rating, and the smallest drive whose rating for the duty, derated for temperature and altitude, carries it is chosen.

bom.intro: List the panel's loads and describe the enclosure. The BOM holds what a sourced table can size: an ACS880-01 drive for each variable-speed load, an outgoing cable for each load, the enclosure, and the cooling it needs by IEC 60890.

line.cooling: Active cooling: {cooling} W beyond what the surface sheds at a {rise} K rise; an air/air heat exchanger needs {qw} W/K

note.incomplete_dissipation: Loads without a heat figure add no heat, so the cooling figure is only as complete as the schedule.
note.not_included: Terminals, and protection for drive-fed and non-motor loads, are not included: no sourced selection table for them is held here.
note.fault_level_assumed: Starters are Type 2 coordinated up to 50 kA; confirm the panel's prospective short-circuit current does not exceed it.
